resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Property Compliance (CPC)
resale_co.issued_by: Department of Housing, Code Enforcement & Rent Leveling (Code Enforcement Office)
requirements: Inspection under the 2015 International Property Maintenance Code (the City's checklist is a general guide, not a full list)
Clean yard, grass and weeds under 10 inches, no rat infestation, sound accessory structures
House number at least 4 inches high
Sound foundation, walls, roof, gutters, chimney, porches, stairs and decks
Windows and doors in good repair and weather tight; screens from April 15 to October 15
Interior surfaces sanitary with no peeling or loose paint or plaster; railings and guards where required
Working plumbing with no leaks; water heater installed right with relief valve and discharge pipe
Heat of at least 65 degrees from October 1 to May 15; fuel-burning appliances vented outside
At least 60 amp electric service, 2 outlets per habitable room, GFCI outlet in bathroom and laundry, cover plates on all outlets
Exit doors and windows openable from inside without keys (no double-keyed deadbolts)
One fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (on the 2021 checklist)
Smoke detectors on every level, in every bedroom and in the hall outside sleeping areas; CO detectors within 10 feet of all bedrooms

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Property Compliance (check 'Seller' and 'SALE APPLICATION', give the buyer and agent details) and file it with the Code Enforcement Office, City Hall, 181 E Commerce Street, Bridgeton, NJ 08302. Call 856-455-3230 (Housing Supervisor ext. 223, Housing Office Clerk ext. 217) to confirm the fee and schedule the inspection.

resale_co.notes: The City's Housing page says a resale Certificate of Property Compliance (CPC) must be filed with the Code Enforcement Office on the sale of any property, and the CPC application has a 'Seller' / 'SALE APPLICATION' box. The only published CPC fee is the Housing page note 'Effective July 14th, 2025 ... First Inspection $35, Re-inspections $18'; the same page says rental CPC fees are covered by the annual rental registration, so the $35 fee most likely applies to sales, but the page does not say so outright. Web search summaries of the City Code on ecode360 (BR1941) mentioned other resale fee amounts, but the code could not be opened and no exact text was seen, so those amounts are not used. No lead time or validity period is published. The CPC application's second page describes the State lead-safe inspection law (P.L.2021, c.182) and lead inspection fees for rental units; that is a rental requirement. Rental registration ($45 per unit by March 1, $75 after) is a rental program, not a resale item.

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter
If there is a fire alarm system, a report from the alarm company is required (per the online application form)

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page, picking Bridgeton City as the municipality. Payment is due at the time of the inspection by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). Re-inspection for a failed or no-show inspection costs the same as the first inspection. The certificate is emailed to the address given and is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 / 856-451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: The City of Bridgeton Fire Department (registry code F) is the local fire enforcing agency and issues the resale smoke/CO certificate through its Bureau of Fire Prevention at 1 Orange Street. Fees, lead time and the 90-day validity come from the Bureau's 'Occupancy & Smoke Certificates' guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025) and match the online application form. The guideline sheet does not list a fire extinguisher (in line with P.L.2025, c.19) but does require 10-year sealed battery alarms and the secondary power source label. The middle fee tier is printed as '7 business days prior'; the gap between 4 and 10 days is not spelled out. Jack Justice Jr.'s email (justicej@cityofbridgeton.com) is linked from his name on the Department page and printed in the state fire directory; the Bureau's general address is firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com.
